sources.title: Phantom Blade Zero: How boss weapons transform combat and exploration
sources.text: A variety of influences come together to create intense action-RPG combat and a strange and fascinating world. Phantom Blade Zero blends influences from a variety of sources to create intense, fast-paced combat and a supernaturally infused Kungfupunk world. It draws on the tough, powerful bosses of Soulslikes, the quick, combo-focused combat of hack-and-slash games, the fascinating stories and characters of RPGs, and the unlockable exploration of search action games. All those ideas come together to create something familiar and unexpected, reworking common action-RPG elements into beautiful, fast-paced battles across a strange, devastated world. While Phantom Blade Zero’s combat evokes games like Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice and Bloodborne, it takes a more hybrid approach, channeling Wuxia stories and kung-fu movies. You’re not just using R1 to dodge, holding L1 to block blows, or tapping L1 to parry them; you also need to press attack, using Square for basic attacks and Triangle for more powerful blows to create simple but effective combos and force your opponent to block and parry as well. It’s all about managing a meter measuring your Sha-Chi. Blocking attacks depletes your Sha-Chi, and if it runs out, you can be staggered and left open to attack — but perfectly parrying, and dodging and landing blows knocks down your opponent’s Sha-Chi instead, letting you cut through their defenses. You can quickly refill your Sha-Chi by pressing Left on the D-Pad to swap between your two equipped main weapons. The system pushes you to string attacks together from both weapons, or to swap as you end your strikes so you’re ready to start parrying. As you land attacks, you also earn Sha-Chi Essence. When it’s fully charged, you can unleash a Power Surge attack with L2 that overpowers your opponent, interrupts their attacks, and deals massive damage. All those elements, combined with powerful Phantom Edge weapons that have specific but limited uses, work together to turn battles into a fluid dance that constantly moves between attack and defense. And thanks to haptic feedback in the DualSense controller, you feel those clashing blades, adding intensity that shows how powerful and lethal their blows can be. One of the best parts of Phantom Blade Zero is the way it dishes out new weapons. Instead of finding swords in treasure chests or buying them from merchants, you claim most of your weapons from bosses you defeat. You get to see exactly how a weapon works as you defend against its unique capabilities, then try those capabilities yourself. For instance, after you defeat the boss Hua, Deadly Betrothed, you can claim her Scarlet Wraithblade, which summons spider lilies on the ground as you complete combos that slow down enemies and let you control the battlefield. The White Serpent and Crimson Viper are dual-wielded swords, and you can use each one’s separate combo, or mix them together for different effects that let you use one sword up close and send the other spinning in circles around you. Each weapon offers its own fighting style, special combos, and status effects, like causing enemies to bleed for extra damage or allowing you to siphon their life. With so many varied combat options, you’ll constantly want to try different weapons and see how they exploit the weaknesses of the tough bosses you’ll face. Exploration is also a big part of the experience. The game is full of side quests and stories to chase down that flesh out the Wulin, the game’s world, and the characters you meet along the way. Each area you visit is expansive, with lots of side paths and secrets to find. Often, you’ll come across areas you can’t reach yet, encouraging you to backtrack later after finding an essential item. Some paths are blocked by specific Phantom Edge weapons that you’ll earn from defeating bosses, making it possible to smash through a barrier or grapple up to a distant location. Phantom Blade Zero ties its storytelling, exploration, and combat together by rewarding you for your curiosity. Exploring new areas will often advance old side quests and uncover new ones. Discovering Blue Memory Flowers scattered throughout the world gives you glimpses into the past that unlock the stories of the places you visit. Finding all the flowers for a given story also increases Soul’s health, making him more powerful for the next battle. The Kungfupunk aesthetic informs not only how Phantom Blade Zero looks, but also the stories you find within it — it’s a dark place, constantly steeped in tragedy. Those stories lead to epic, varied boss fights against powerful martial artists and corrupted, monstrous characters. Hua, Deadly Betrothed, is an early optional boss who forces you to stay aware of your surroundings as she summons deadly spider lilies that sap your strength and stagger you, leaving you open to massive blows from her huge sword. Once you defeat her, you learn about how she was used by the man she was to marry, and her rage resulted in the massacre of the entire wedding party. Other characters represent the powers hunting Soul throughout the game, whose motivations are slowly uncovered through flashbacks as you push forward. Jing Ye, The Outlaw, comes at you on horseback and employs dirty tricks, throwing dirt in your face to obscure your vision as he tries to run you down. When you finally knock him off his mount, he comes at you with a spiked shield that damages you when you attack, and a huge sword he’ll try to bury in your flesh to absorb your blood and heal himself. And then there are characters with their own agendas, like the Gold-Masked One, a man you encounter in the strange illusory realm of the Discordance, played by actor and martial arts legend Donnie Yen. As you learn more about his shadowed story, he challenges you to vicious duels, using sword slashes, kicks, punches, and powerful, unblockable throws to rip through your life meter. sources.title: Phantom Blade Zero Sells 4 Million Copies in 72 Hours
sources.text: Phantom Blade Zero is officially the next big thing. Developer S-Game has announced that its wuxia-themed action game has surpassed a significant milestone in just a few days. Within 72 hours of going on sale, Phantom Blade Zero has sold 4 million copies. The official X / Twitter account posted the news with a message: “Thank you everyone from the bottom of our hearts for all the love and support!” Even on its first day, it was clear this was going to be a beast. Phantom Blade Zero was ahead of Steam’s biggest games , from PUBG to Dota 2, topping the Steam charts as soon as it launched. It was also the best-selling game on Steam by revenue, ahead of Modern Warfare 4, Aion 2, and Probably Stolen, a Cyberpunk shopkeeper sim that's going viral. Steam concurrents peaked on Sunday with a whopping 833,921 players. The early success shouldn't come as a huge surprise. Last week, it was estimated that Phantom Blade Zero had sold over 1 million copies before launch across launch platforms Steam and PS5, and Tencent’s WeGame (an online PC storefront in China). Nearly two thirds of total prelaunch sales were from China, Taiwan, or Hong Kong. IGN's Phantom Blade Zero review returned a 9/10. We said: "Phantom Blade Zero is an unbelievably smooth action game filled with memorable boss fights, compelling combat, and limitless swagger." Phantom Blade Zero is a monster hit, but it's not quite on par with Black Myth: Wukong, which managed 10 million sales in the first three days . Roger Craig Smith — best known as Sonic the Hedgehog, Ezio Auditore, Batman, and Chris Redfield — plays the lead character. The actor is joined by Mu Xiaokui actor Maggie Robertson, who played Lady Dimitrescu in Resident Evil 7. Elsewhere in the cast, Donnie Yen served as a key creative consultant and stars as the character Mó Yuan (Soul's father) through full facial, voice, and motion capture. Before you step into the Phantom World, we’ve put together a helpful list of Things Phantom Blade Zero Doesn’t Tell You . We’ve also got a step-by-step Phantom Blade Zero Walkthrough in progress, plus guides for the game’s Weapons , Accessories , and Phantom Edges . Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

sources.title: Phantom Blade Zero is Steam's biggest launch of the year so far, selling over 4 million copies in three days
sources.text: Phantom Blade Zero studio S-Game has announced that its debut title has sold more than 4m copies in its first 72 hours on sale. The game's official X account broke the news alongside a celebratory message, though without providing a per-platform breakdown of copies sold. "Thank you everyone from the bottom of our hearts for all the love and support!" the developer wrote on X . Phantom Blade Zero is available on Steam and PlayStation 5, but the 4m figure also includes sales made on the China-exclusive Tencent WeGame PC launcher. Prior to launch, Alinea Analytics analyst Rhys Elliott estimated Phantom Blade Zero to have sold over 1m copies before it had even released . It was always clear the third-person character action game was going to be a hit, we just had to wait for actual figures to be released. Phantom Blade Zero attracted over 431,000 concurrent players on Steam at launch, a figure that kept risking and rising into the weekend, ultimately settling at a massive 833,921 peak concurrent (via SteamDB ). Just in case it wasn't already clear, this is Steam's biggest launch of the year so far, beating the likes of Forza Horizon 6 and far outpacing all other major releases such as Onimusha: Way of the Sword , The Blood of Dawnwalker , and Ace Combat 8 . Despite the very strong opening weekend's numbers, Phantom Blade Zero has not been able to match or exceed the performance of Black Myth: Wukong , 2024's also-Chinese developed triple-A action game, just yet. The breakout hit, estimated to have sold 30m copies since , is one of Steam's largest debuts ever, peaking at 2,415,714 concurrent players at launch. In Eurogamer's Phantom Blade Zero review , Emma Kent spoke highly of much of the game, but was critical of its underwhelming narrative and lack of consistency, writing: "This game is exceptional in so many areas - the animations, the beautiful environments - and when the combat works, the sense of flow is incredible. Then you walk into a boss battle and feel all that power fade, like you're waiting your turn to get hits in with a wooden sword."

sources.name: Insider Gaming
sources.title: Phantom Blade Zero Sells 4 Million Copies In 72 Hours
sources.text: Phantom Blade Zero has sold over 4 million copies across all available platforms within the first 72 hours of its release, marking a monumental achievement for developer S-Game . Available on PC and PlayStation 5 , the action-RPG represents the studio’s first major release outside of mobile gaming, and it’s already proving to be another huge success story for Chinese game development. The game is attracting plenty of attention from both fans and critics alike, with its launch sales figures highlighting just how popular it’s become. The impressive sales figures for Phantom Blade Zero were shared directly by the development team, with the studio taking to social media to celebrate the milestone just three days after launch. With over 4 million copies sold, it’s hardly surprising to see the game’s player counts continue to climb on Steam. Phantom Blade Zero is edging closer to the one million concurrent players mark , having reached a peak of 830,000 players at the time of writing. That’s an impressive figure in its own right, especially when you consider that it doesn’t include the PlayStation 5 player base. The game’s success has also sparked comparisons to Black Myth: Wukong, another major Chinese-developed release that sold 10 million copies within the same timeframe. Wukong arguably helped establish one of the biggest success stories for Chinese single-player games in the Western market, and Phantom Blade Zero appears to be following a similar trajectory. Given that S-Game has made a conscious effort to appeal to a Western audience , these early sales figures suggest that the studio’s ambitions have paid off in a big way. It’s also worth noting that Phantom Blade Zero comes in at a lower price point than many traditional AAA releases , while offering a substantial amount of content and playtime . With that in mind, its early commercial success shouldn’t come as too much of a surprise. Have you picked up Phantom Blade Zero? Let us know your thoughts on the Insider Gaming Discord server . stories.title: Persona 1 Remake Footage Seemingly Leaks Online
stories.summary: What appears to be gameplay footage from an unannounced Persona 1 remake has leaked online.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Persona 1 Remake Footage Seemingly Leaks Online
sources.text: What appears to be gameplay footage from an unannounced Persona 1 remake has leaked online. A little less than two minutes of video depicting what looks like a modern version of Sega and Atlus' original Persona game was first shared by a YouTube channel using the name P1REMAKE and was eventually picked up across social media platforms like Reddit . The YouTube account it's tied to was created in March 2010 and has seemingly posted just two other videos, with its previous upload published more than 14 years ago. The developers behind the RPG franchise have broached the topic of remakes for early installments in the past but never confirmed work was underway, meaning this could be our first look at the series' next remake. In the age of AI-generated fakes, you can never be too skeptical about things like this, but fans generally seem to be under the impression that the footage is authentic. While we won't share it here, you don't have to look too hard to see what everyone's talking about. Yea that Persona 1 remake leaked footage gotta be 100% real. I refuse to believe someone would do that much work to make a fake leak. There are a few reasons players suspect this to be our first glimpse at a not-so-secret Persona 1 remake from Atlus. Aside from the music, effects, and art, which all fall right in line with much of the studio's recent work, the video on display is much longer and more detailed than any fake leak would typically be. The smoking gun for many, though, is the character animations. It's specifically Eriko that people are calling out, as she seems to share a summoning animation with Persona 4 Revival 's version of Yukiko. Atlus' Persona 4 remake, of course, won't be out until February 18, 2027. There's also the issue of the appearance of Persona 2 protagonist Tatsuya, who seems to be standing in for what may be an unfinished character model. So, what can we make of all of this? Well, unfortunately, without confirmation from Sega or Atlus, not much. There is always the chance this could be an elaborate fake, with some of these odd details serving as evidence for that argument. On the other hand, it's possible placeholder assets and familiar animations are here specifically because the alleged Persona 1 remake is still very much in development. Persona 1 leak looks credible, not sure why people are reporting Tatsuya is replacing Masao, that's just complete bogus. This is most likely an internal investor pitch for remakes of Persona 1 and 2, and not actually Persona 1. There are Persona 4 Revival animations in the gameplay footage, which definitely helps the case of it being real. That sure is a persona 1 remake trailer. Why is tatsuya there We don't know when this footage would have been captured, even if it does turn out to be real. That means this could be from yesterday or years ago, with some speculating that the video we've seen today is little more than a proof-of-concept or pitch video. If the Persona: Be Your True Mind remake footage is authentic, it wouldn't be the biggest surprise to see it announced. Sega released its Persona 3 remake, Persona 3 Reload , in 2024, and will release Persona 4 Revival in just a few months. Atlus' P-Studio producer, Kazuhisa Wada, stopped short of confirming development for Persona 1 and 2 remakes in August of this year but still admitted that, as far as he's concerned, it's something "we have to do." Meanwhile, Atlus has absolutely suffered leaks before. The Persona 3 remake had in-development footage questioned by fans when it showed up online back in 2023. The upcoming Persona 6 , which, officially, we've seen little of so far, had images leak in June. A massive Steam leak in September then seemingly revealed a list of trophies – including story spoilers – for the upcoming installment. Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

sources.name: Gematsu
sources.title: Rumor: Persona remake footage appears online
sources.text: A video reel showcasing what appears to be work-in-progress footage of a Revelations: Persona remake has surfaced online. The footage, a showreel similar to the one showcasing footage of Persona 3 Reload that leaked prior to its announcement, features three sections of the game—field, battle, and event scenes built around 2D illustrations. Persona 2: Innocent Sin protagonist Tatsuya Suou appears in the battle section of the footage. However, since he does not appear in Revelations: Persona , he may be a stand-in for another character. It’is also possible that remakes of Persona 2: Innocent Sin and / or Persona 2: Eternal Punishment are simultaneously in development. Other things worth noting are the constant appearance of Unreal Engine debut text in the upper-left corner of the screen and the fact that Eriko Kirishima appears to use the same Persona summon animation as Yukiko Amagi in Persona 4 Revival , lending the footage further credibility. As for the source of the footage, it was originally posted to YouTube by a user named “P1REMAKE” today at 2:25 a.m. PT / 5:25 a.m. ET . As of press time, the YouTube video remains accessible, but copies have also been hosted on file-sharing websites such as Gofile and Catbox , and shared in communities like r/GamingLeaksAndRumours . The YouTube account was created in March 2010 and has only ever posted two other videos, though its username was likely changed to “P1REMAKE” around the time the footage was posted.

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: Two minutes of Persona 1 remake footage seemingly leaks online
sources.text: Two minutes of footage from an unannounced turn-based RPG recently spilled online, and yep, it very much looks like a remake of the very first Persona game. A YouTube account aptly called 'P1REMAKE' only yesterday posted a little under two minutes of footage from what appears to be a Persona 1 remake. As expected, eagle-eyed fans quickly spotted the clip and soon spread it across several other social media platforms, with the footage since appearing on Reddit and X. Of course, you should take all leaks with an unhealthily huge handful of salt no matter how convincing they look - especially in the age of generative-AI videos and such. At the same time, there are quite a few good reasons to let yourself be a little hopeful for this remake. For one, the two-minute clip is longer and more elaborate than gen-AI videos typically are. Several series fans have also pointed out the video shows Eriko summoning her Persona in combat, while using the exact same animation as Persona 4 Revival's version of bestie Yukiko. Revival doesn't actually launch until next year, which makes the pose quite suspicious. Then there's the fact that this type of leak isn't exactly new territory for Atlus' popular role-playing franchise. In 2023, footage from what ended up being called Persona 3 Reload leaked online and showed very similarly rough, clearly in-development scenes from the game's dungeons. One other curiosity is the inclusion of Tatsuya, the protagonist from Persona 2 Innocent Sin, who doesn't actually show up in the series' first game. Some folks are speculating that the video might have been created as an internal proof-of-concept pitch for Sega and Atlus management, so Tatsuya would serve as a placeholder model in that case. A Persona 1 remake isn't entirely unlikely with or without this potential leak, either. Persona series producer Kazuhisa Wada recently said remakes of the first two games are "probably eventually" happening at some point in the future. sources.title: Footage of a Persona 1 remake has seemingly leaked online
sources.text: Almost two minutes of footage from what appears to be a remake of the original Persona has leaked online. The clip, which seemingly gives the remake the subtitle Be Your True Mind, was shared on the GamingLeaksAndRumours subreddit . It was uploaded to file-sharing site Gofile on 31st October under a Japanese filename that translates as "Megami Ibunroku Persona Remake". Interestingly, the footage looks a lot like Atlus' more recent entries. It shows off stylish menus and a brief look at combat that closely resembles Persona 5 and Persona 3 Reload . There's also a short social link cutscene in a noticeably different, almost graphic novel art style. Fans digging through the clip believe they have spotted several details that lend it credibility. These include what looks like Unreal Engine debug text in the top left corner during battle (Atlus switched to Unreal Engine for Persona 3 Reload), a new remix of the original PlayStation game's Pandora theme, and the protagonist being referred to as "Boy With Earring", which is how he is named in Persona 2: Eternal Punishment . Atlus has not announced a Persona 1 remake, and we can't verify the footage, so treat all of this with the usual caveats. How do you solve a problem like Persona 4 ? At Gamescom, we sat down with series director Kazuhisa Wada to talk about the Persona 4 Remake , and ask about how Atlus is approaching the original text for the remake.

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: Footage of what sure looks like a Persona 1 remake has leaked
sources.text: Persona tragics have been begging for remakes of the first two games in the series for ages (at least, the ones who aren't begging for remakes of the PS2-era Shin Megami Tensei games instead). After thoroughly milking Persona 4 and 5, series producer Kazuhisa Wada said in August , "personally, I think it's something we should definitely do." Now, almost two minutes of footage from what sure looks like a Persona 1 remake has leaked via the GamingLeaksAndRumours subreddit . It shows some dungeon exploration, typically flashy combat, and a dialogue scene all in the modern Persona style. Oddly, Tatsuya from Persona 2 is one of the party members, though it's possible this is a cross-promotional skin you can equip. Or maybe the remakes will incorporate some kind of Persona Q-style crossover? While it's fair to be suspicious this could be AI-generated footage, it seems both a bit too long and too internally consistent for that to be the case. And it's not like Atlus hasn't got form, given that we found out the Persona 3 remake was real via a leak as well. stories.title: Yakuza Series Creator Toshiro Nagoshi's Studio Has Officially Shut Down Before Releasing a Game
stories.summary: Yakuza series creator Toshiro Nagoshi’s studio has officially shut down before it had the chance to release a game.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Yakuza Series Creator Toshiro Nagoshi's Studio Has Officially Shut Down Before Releasing a Game
sources.text: Yakuza series creator Toshiro Nagoshi’s studio has officially shut down before it had the chance to release a game. Gematsu reported that the Tokyo-based Nagoshi Studio closed its doors via a shareholders’ resolution on October 31. The announcement was made in today’s Japanese government gazette Kanpo. The Yakuza-like Gang of Dragon was meant to be the debut game from Nagoshi Studio, which Nagoshi formed in 2022 with investment from Chinese megacorp NetEase after he departed Ryu Ga Gotoku a year earlier. But doubt was cast on its future in March when NetEase signalled its intention to cut off funding as part of a broader retreat from international video game investment. According to Bloomberg , NetEase made the decision to cut Nagoshi’s funding after it learned Gang of Dragon needed at least another ¥7 billion (approx. $44.4 million) to be completed. Nagoshi was apparently trying to find new investors to help buy the studio out, without much luck. The studio closes nearly a year after Gang of Dragon enjoyed a flashy reveal at The Game Awards in December . Now, it looks like it may never see the light of day. sources.title: Nagoshi Studio Officially Shut Down One Year After The Game Awards Reveal
sources.text: Nagoshi Studio, the all-new venture established by Toshihiro Nagoshi, a former 30-year veteran of Sega, has officially been dissolved by NetEase, Japanese media has revealed. In March, it was revealed that NetEase had halted funding for the studio, directly impacting the ongoing development of GANG OF DRAGON, the team’s debut title. The game had been given a grand reveal during 2025’s The Game Awards showcase, and it was met with a positive reception. Unfortunately, barely one year later, it has been reported that Nagoshi Studio is officially closed. It was revealed earlier this year that GANG OF DRAGON would require tens of millions of dollars to be finished. That was a request that NetEase was unwilling to satisfy, and per the report, they pulled the plug on funding . The Japanese government’s Official Gazette , published on November 2nd, has confirmed that Nagoshi Studio has been officially dissolved, barely five years after it was founded by Toshihiro Nagoshi, former chief creative officer at Sega and creator of the Yakuza series. It was stated that the decision to shut down Nagoshi Studio was made on October 31st, and now, a liquidation process has started that will see the company’s assets and liabilities settled. The future of GANG OF DRAGON is now entirely unclear but likely unrecoverable. At the time of writing, GANG OF DRAGON’s Steam page was still accessible, listing the game as ‘coming soon’. It was set to be an action-adventure title set to rival everything Yakuza had come to be, set in the heart of modern-day Tokyo and featuring a stellar cast. Were you looking forward to GANG OF DRAGON? Let us know your thoughts about this news on the Insider Gaming Discord server . sources.name: GamesIndustry.biz
sources.title: Gang of Dragon developer Nagoshi Studio shutters months after NetEase cut funding
sources.text: Studio was "officially dissolved by a shareholders' resolution" on October 31, 2026 Gang of Dragon developer Nagoshi Studio has been closed after NetEase withdrew funding earlier this year. According to Gematsu , the Japanese government gazette Kanpo published a closure notice on October 31, stating the studio was "officially dissolved by a shareholders' resolution." Yakuza series creator Toshihiro Nagoshi founded Nagoshi Studio under NetEase Games in 2022 . In December 2025, the studio debuted a teaser trailer for its new IP, Gang of Dragon, at The Game Awards. By March 2026, NetEase confirmed it had cut funding to the studio but did not disclose reasons or exit terms. Reports indicated NetEase estimated "at least ¥7 billion ($44.4 million) more would be needed" for Nagoshi Studio to complete Gang of Dragon. The developer reportedly "tried to find new sponsors without success" and NetEase told it that "while it is free to continue on its own, it must bear the corresponding costs if it wants to keep the assets or brand." Nagoshi joined Sega in 1989 and spent several years in the AM2 arcade division. He later served as chief creative officer at Sega until 2021, after stepping down from the board . Nagoshi continued at Sega as creative director and was also general director of Like a Dragon developer Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio. Nagoshi Studio is not the only Japanese developer to have ended its partnership with NetEase. In September, Romeo is a Dead Man Grasshopper Manufacture split from the China-based publisher to become independent . CEO Goichi 'Suda51' Suda said the studio "found a strong desire to deliver titles in an even wider variety of styles to video game lovers everywhere," which led it to become independent again. "This decision was reached after thorough discussions with NetEase Games and with their generous cooperation. We continue to cherish the amazing relationship our companies have built, and look forward to further collaboration when the opportunity arises."

sources.name: Gematsu
sources.title: Nagoshi Studio shuts down
sources.text: Nagoshi Studio , the Shinjuku, Tokyo-based founded by Yakuza series creator Toshiro Nagoshi under NetEase Games in November 2021, was officially dissolved by a shareholders’ resolution on October 31, according to a notice published in today’s Japanese government gazette Kanpo . In December 2025, Nagoshi Studio announced GANG OF DRAGON , a Kabukicho-set action adventure game starring Korean actor Ma Dong-seok (Don Lee). In March 2026, Bloomberg reported that NetEase Games planned to cut funding from the studio in May, and that it had the option to go independent if it was able to pay its way out.

Nagoshi Studio was formed in 2021 and its debut title, Gang of Dragon, was announced in December and said to be âdeep into developmentâ. The action game stared prolific South Korean-American actor Ma Dong-seok, best known for his performances in Train to Busan, The Outlaws, and Marvelâs Eternals. According to an earlier Bloomberg report, employees of Nagoshi Studio were told in March that publisher NetEase intended to cut off funding for the project. NetEase allegedly made the decision after discovering that the project needed an additional Â¥7 billion ($44.4 million) in funding to reach completion. In Nagoshi Studioâs first Western interview in 2023, Â Nagoshi told VGC Â that he would not let down fans of his previous games and would ensure they would be happy with his new studioâs debut game. Nagoshi Studio is the latest casualty of NetEaseâs decision to significantly scale back its international game development operations, following years of investment in new studios around the world. The move has caused chaos across its international operations, with several studios being forced to close, and others seeking new funding. In addition to the initial closure of T-Minus, FPC, and Bad Brain, NetEaseÂ split from Vancouver-based Worlds Untold , the studio it founded with Mass Effect writerÂ Mac Â Walters in 2023,Â as well as Seattle-based Jar of Sparks , the studio founded in 2022 byÂ Xbox Â veteran Jerry Hook. Ouka Studio, the Tokyo-based developer behind Square Enix âs Visions of Mana, was also closed in 2024. Other Japanese studios, like Goichi Suda âs Grasshopper Manufacture and Resident Evil producer Hiroyuki Kobayashiâs GPTRACK50 , have pushed ahead with new games without NetEase funding.

sources.text: Pre-orders open on World of Warcraft: Forever's release date Final Fantasy 14 : Evercold has received a short and swift four-week delay. Square Enix 's MMORPG expansion was originally set to release in January of next year, but an update from Final Fantasy Fan Fest Japan has revealed that it's now due to come out during the packed month of February, 2027. Final Fantasy 14 boss Naoki Yoshida - affectionately dubbed Yoshi-P by fans - revealed the news during FF14 Fan Fest Japan. Evercold's new release date is officially February 23, 2027 with an early access period beginning on February 19, 2027. Of course, February is already packed with mammoth games - everything from Fable, God of War: Laufey, Persona 4 Revival, and Metro 2039 are seemingly taking shelter from GTA 6 . Here's hoping you have a spare few dozen hours a week for all the incoming goodies. Evercold pre-orders begin on November 4, which is funnily enough the official release date of Final Fantasy 14's biggest rival: World of Warcraft Forever. ( I'm sure it's just coincidental .) Pre-order bonuses include a Kottr minion that's part of the expansion's new, fluffy, feline race, as well as a pair of earrings and early access. You can check out all the different editions over on the official website - be warned, the Final Fantasy 13 mount might tempt you to put a dent in your wallet. Evercold makes a ton of changes to the beloved, widely played online game. For one, a new Evolved system is promising to streamline ability hotbars and rejig the way jobs work. The game's also crossing over with the Final Fantasy 7 Remake series in a new Evercold raid. sources.title: Final Fantasy 14 Evercold Gets A Month Long Delay But An Awesome New Trailer
sources.text: Delay Evercold Final Fantasy XIV MMORPG Trailer There was good and bad news at Final Fantasy XIV ‘s Japan Fan Fest . The bad news was that the MMORPG’s new expansion Evercold has been delayed by about a month. Originally set for sometime in January, the full launch will now arrive on February 23, 2027. The good news is that Evercold now has its third and final teaser trailer, a six minute cinematic that sets up the narrative stakes for Final Fantasy XIV ‘s biggest update in nearly three years. “Tell me about the Promised Land,” a young girl asks early in the trailer. A wise old lady recalls a time of beauty and abundance that gave way to a “relentless ice” as magical beasts took over the mainland. People abandoned the continent for the skies above. The rest of the trailer is pretty much a ton of breathless views of massive city-sized airships (called Realmships) and cool battles showing off new job classes like the tanky Bastion who wields gunshields called Skyltborgs. Something that Square Enix doesn’t get enough credit for in its fantasy world building style is sneaking guns into stuff and making it look elegant and cool as hell. The trailer also showed off the new DPS class called Zephyr, which wields a cross bow and a neat bird companion. It received its own breakout trailer giving fans a quick lowdown on how it will work. In fact, there were a lot of trailers to come out of the Japan Fan Fest. We got another teaser for the Neon Evangalion crossover event coming in 2027 as well as deep dives into the new locations and other changes coming with version 8.0 in Evercold . It will give players plenty to chew on as they wait a month longer for the full release. Pre-orders for Evercold open on November 4, 2026 (there’s a trailer for the collector’s edition, too ). Those who pay for the pre-order (any edition) will get early access to the expansion starting Friday, February 19, 2027. While a four week delay isn’t a big deal, this does mean that February is now even more packed. Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis , God of War Laufey , Persona 4 Revival , and Fable all come out within a week of Evercold ‘s early access window. Should be fun! sources.title: Fan-made Oblivion remake Skyblivion runs into legal trouble with a former volunteer
sources.text: "A 'take your ball and go home' approach like this fundamentally contradicts the collaborative, open spirit of the modding community" Skyblivion (the fan-made Oblivion remake that's being rebuilt inside of Skyrim) has been a long time coming, but we might need to wait a while longer for the conversion mod to see the light of day due to a new legal issue. One of the ambitious project's lead modders, Rebelzize, today uploaded a video about the ongoing situation. "Recently, a former volunteer who contributed to Skyblivion's development departed the project. We want to be completely transparent with the community about what has happened since their departure," he explains in the description. "After they left the project, we had several discussions regarding the continued use and maintenance of his work. The main disagreement centered on their objection to our decompilation of parts of their work — a necessary step our team took to maintain functionality and fix issues in systems already built into the project after access to the original source code repository was revoked," Rebelzize adds. Rebelzize doesn't name the former modder in an effort to avoid creating an online "witch hunt," but they eventually sent the Skyblivion folks a series of legal threats demanding the real names and home addresses of several other volunteer team members - "something that we are simply not willing to share with somebody that we don't even know," Rebelzize says, calling the demands "disproportionate." The former modder is apparently looking to sue for damages worth upwards of €30,000. "A 'take your ball and go home' approach like this fundamentally contradicts the collaborative, open spirit of the modding community that makes massive passion projects like this possible," Rebelzize continues. "To protect our volunteers from undue stress and ensure a clean break, in good faith we removed their code, rebuilding and improving the system from the ground up." Despite removing their work from Skyblivion, the anonymous former volunteer has apparently "continued to intensify their threats." The Skyblivion team is now looking for help from anyone experienced in IP and GDPR law, pointing interested folks toward their official website . Last year, it looked like a Skyblivion release date could be right around the corner . There's still no word on when we can expect the gorgeous fan-led revival, though. sources.title: Team Behind Fan-Made Oblivion Remake Face Lawsuit From Former Contributor
sources.text: Bethesda Fan game The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Since 2012, a team of Elder Scrolls fans have been assembling a total conversion of Oblivion to run off the engine of its descendant, Skyrim . Known as “ Skyblivion ” the fan-project has spent over a decade in development. While a lengthy development is often filled with ups and downs, its latest woe is a rather unique one, as developers say that one of their former members is threatening litigation . “Recently, a former volunteer who contributed to Skyblivion âs development departed the project,” posted The Elder Scrolls Renewal Project . “We want to be completely transparent with the community about what has happened since their departure.” A former volunteer is attempting to sue Skyblivion and we need your help pic.twitter.com/3Ee5eQTELG — Skyblivion (@TESRSkyblivion) October 30, 2026 According to the statement, an unnamed volunteer contributor left the team a short time ago. Since leaving, there has been a great deal of contention around the work they left behind. The former developer, according to the post, objected to the “decompilation of parts of their work,” something bound to happen as other aspects are reworked and improved. In response, the disgruntled party sent a legal threat, demanding the real names of others involved. To temper the situation, the statement says they decided to remove the code and contributions in question, but despite that the former member has “continued to intensify their threats.” In a video plea , Kyle Rebel says that one anonymous community member demanding the legal names of the others is unacceptable. In kind, they also ask supporters not to”make this a witch-hunt,” requesting pro-bono legal assistance and resources over any online campaign to sniff out the unnamed troll. The nature of their contributions, the reasons for their departure, and what contractual agreements were made (if any) are left unspecified. “A “take your ball and go home” approach like this fundamentally contradicts the collaborative, open spirit of the modding community that makes massive passion projects like this possible,” reads the statement. “While weâve consulted with legal counsel and are completely confident in our right to maintain the code they submitted, we had zero interest in holding onto friction or fighting a former team member.” Skyblivion has become something of a Ship of Theseus. Originally aimed to be a direct port, work generally evolved into something closer to a hide-to-hair remake that would be implemented as a Steam mod. While anonymous, the team of hobby developers is estimated to have grown to around 40 strong. They had aimed for a 2025 release, though by the end of the year they admitted it would need more time. Obviously another hurdle was the release of Bethesdaâs own remastered Oblivion that same year, though the community said it wouldnât stop their efforts . Fan-projects are no strangers to legal threats, many having to bow out or become entirely new when the official studios rattle their tail. In this case, however, Bethesda was vocally supportive of Skyblivion , and the litigation has come from within. Donât miss the latest reviews, news and tips. Sign up for our free newsletter. sources.title: Doom Director Says ‘We’re Doing Great’ After Half Of id Software Was Laid Off
sources.text: Doom: The Dark Ages Id Software MachineGames Wolfenstein 3 Xbox’s summer reset hit a lot of storied game studios very hard. Among them was id Software, the long-running maker of the iconic Doom franchise. Roughly half the studio was canned just 24 hours before it launched its big expansion to Doom: The Dark Ages . Questions have swirled about the studio’s future and what it will still be capable of after deep cuts to important departments that scattered decades of combined institutional knowledge. According to studio co-director Marty Stratton, things are still going swimmingly . “We’re doing great,” he reportedly told media at a press event earlier this week when asked about the impact of the layoffs, according to IGN . “Not to handwave the [layoffs] away…everybody knows we had about half of our studio exit as part of that. But there was a very deliberate effort to make sure that we were incredibly viable coming out of that across everything we do, across game development and technology department.” Big “My ‘incredibly viable studio’ T-shirt has people asking a lot of questions already answered by my shirt” energy. One of the big asterisks for id Software coming out of the brutal Xbox reset was the long-term sustainability of id Tech , the proprietary game engine upon which the studio’s world class first-person shooters are built. “It is hard to make a game that is AAA thatâs like weâve done before with half the people,” Chris Hays, a veteran programmer at the company, said in August . “And by hard I mean impossible.â Id Software has previously pushed back on those claims, arguing that the studio is about where it was when it was shipping Doom 2016 nearly a decade ago.Â MachineGames, which is working on the unannounced Wolfenstein 3 , uses a different fork of id Tech for its projects. One suggestion has been that both studios could pool their remaining engineering sources to try to bridge the gap for future releases. “We’re working more closely with MachineGames than ever,” Stratton reportedly told media this week. “We’ve always had a very close partnership with them, but I think we’re at a point with technology development that both teams are incredibly talented and have incredibly talented engineers and we’re really on an amazing path that had started pre-[layoffs]. We’d kicked this off earlier this year. We’re really excited about that. We’re both really really bullish on what we have ahead.” Xbox has about a quarter of its “reset” left to go, with additional rounds of layoffs reportedly scheduled for November and January. It remains to be seen what Microsoft’s plans are for franchises like Doom in the future. Donât miss the latest reviews, news and tips. Sign up for our free newsletter. sources.title: id Software co-director says the Doom developer is 'working more closely with MachineGames than ever' after Xbox laid off 'about half of our studio'
sources.text: MachineGames is rumoured to be working on a third Wolfenstein game. Id Software has tightened its relationship with fellow shooter specialists MachineGames according to studio co-director Marty Stratton, after Xbox laid off roughly half of the Doom developer's employees earlier this year. Stratton was asked how the studio was doing following Xbox's massive job cuts at a recent press event for Doom: The Dark Ages' Revelations DLC (via IGN ) and he was keen to assure everyone that things are hunky dory at the legendary FPS developer. "We're doing great," Stratton explained. "Not to handwave the [layoffs] away … everybody knows we had about half of our studio exit as part of that. But there was a very deliberate effort to make sure that we were incredibly viable coming out of that across everything we do, across game development and [the] technology department." As part of its response to those layoffs, id Software has apparently deepened its ties with MachineGames, developers of Wolfenstein: The New Order and, more recently, the excellent Indiana Jones and the Great Circle . "We're working more closely with MachineGames than ever," Stratton said. "We've always had a very close partnership with them, but I think we're at the point with technology development that both teams are incredibly talented and have incredibly talented engineers and we're really on an amazing path that had started pre-[layoffs]. We'd kicked this off earlier this year. We're really excited about that. We're both really, really bullish on what we have ahead. Stratton's comments have led to speculation that the two developers may be cooperating on Wolfenstein 3, which MachineGames is rumoured to be working on . Id Software has just concluded active development of Doom: The Dark Ages following the expansions' release, so this is possible. What's interesting to me, however, is how Stratton repeatedly references technology. The id Software layoffs heavily impact the developer's Frankfurt arm, including numerous designers of the formidable id-tech engine. This led to fears that id-tech was being shelved. Microsoft contradicted this, though further reports left the question open . But Stratton's comments lead me to believe we might be seeing a tech alignment between the two developers as a result of those Frankfurt layoffs. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. While id Software built Doom: The Dark Ages on id-tech 8, MachineGames used a modified version of id-tech 7, called Motor, for Indiana Jones and the Great Circle. The fact that Stratton references both teams' "incredibly talented engineers" suggests to me that id Software is folding MachineGames' engine programmers directly into id-tech's ongoing development, with both teams working on the engine concurrently going forward. Assuming that id tech hasn't been canned outright, this approach would make sense given the expertise id Software lost from its Frankfurt arm. Sadly, the layoffs that affected id Software were far from the last at Xbox. After cutting 1600 jobs in the summer, Xbox initiated a second wave of layoffs in September that also saw Obsidian and Bethesda merge and put Activision in charge of Halo. Further Xbox layoffs are planned leading up to January 2027, while Microsoft more broadly has offered a "voluntary exit offer" to over a quarter of its workforce. 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex. Between 2013 and 2022, Rick was games editor of Custom PC magazine and associated website bit-tech.net . But he's always kept one foot in freelance games journalism, writing for publications like Edge, Eurogamer, the Guardian and, naturally, PC Gamer. While he'll play anything that can be controlled with a keyboard and mouse, he has a particular passion for first-person shooters and immersive sims. sources.title: Nintendo Reveals Surprise Pikmin Day Direct
sources.text: Nintendo has revealed a surprise Nintendo Direct for Pikmin Day because it has apparently decided that's a thing now. Instead of spooky game announcements or horror movie memes, video game fans woke up to on Halloween 2026 was Mario creator Shigeru Miyamoto's face. That's because Nintendo has declared November 1 as Pikmin Day, and it's got a brand-new Direct to celebrate the occasion. Yes, really. None of this is a joke. There's a little more than nine minutes of announcements to go over. Although there's no Pikmin 5 reveal or anything else too groundbreaking here, Miyamoto did take the time to share new information about Pikmin 4 and promised that, "going forward, I want people to know more about Pikmin." Tomorrow is Pikmin Day! Join in on the fun by playing Pikmin games on Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch. https://t.co/iYxZldya7p So, to start, why is the first of November Pikmin Day? Nintendo's miniaturized franchise launched in Japan in October 2001 before coming to North America in December, so there's no tie to a release date like you might have guessed. Instead, Miyamoto explained that November 1 is Pikmin Day because there were originally only three Pikmin, which, when standing next to each other, kinda looks like "11.1." Ready to test your skills at Dandori Academy? A free demo of #Pikmin4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy will be available on Nov 2. https://t.co/rNHNq35RMT You gotta give 'em credit for creativity, as Pikmin Day is probably one of the last things anyone expected to see today. Still, it served as a nice opportunity to offer an update on Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy ahead of its release November 12, 2026. Players will be able to use the new consoles built-in microphone to Oatchi, controlling them by using commands like 'rush' and 'go to work.' The Dandori Academy mode, meanwhile, comes with new challenges, including exams that take place on Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays, that give players timed tasks and an opportunity to earn medals. A demo for the Switch 2 version of Pikimin 4 will be available starting November 2, with save data available to transfer to the full launch. It offers access to the Sun-Speckled Terrace opening area, as well as two Dandori Academy stages. Secret Caves are coming this winter! Get ready to explore Secret Caves, face off against familiar creatures, and uncover hidden treasures along the way in @PikminBloom on your smartphone. https://t.co/Nx6Lzba6v4 Nintendo first brought its augmented-reality game, Pikmin Bloom, to smartphone devices in 2021, but five years on, and it's still got more to give. As shown in a teaser video featuring a group of the colorful plant-like creatures battling a Bulborb, an update scheduled to arrive this winter will add a new mechanic called Secret Caves. These battle-focused exploration events allow players to take their crew into caves to battle creatures and earn rewards. Before a cave is explored, players must collect a cave map, which feature information about a cave and can be found on things like Postcards. Then, Pikmin are sent into the cave to search for treasures, with some of the items highlighted during the Direct including a rubber duck, a sword, a cookie, and a chef hat. Should a battle ensue, you'll command your army by sending them in to attack when the moment is right, or retreat if things get too hairy. Pikmin 4's Dandori Academy challenges also give players an opportunity to collect maps by taking exams. If you couldn't tell from the video games, shorts , and Easter Eggs Nintendo has highlighted through the franchise's 25-year history, it's got a soft spot for Pikmin. Miyamoto has spearheaded this charge, and because he wants people to know more about the company's adorable little mascots, he's enlisted some help. Joining him during the Nintendo Direct broadcast was Japanese actress and crafty Pikmin fan Fuka Koshiba. Known for her work on TV projects like Siren and films like Lady Kaga, Miyamoto brought her in to help him "build more excitement around Pikmin going forward" after she shared hand-made Pikmin-themed hats on Instagram. "Originally, I had heard on social media that you could get hats of the Red Pikmin, Blue Pikmin, and Yellow Pikmin from those claw machines," Koshiba said, holding one of her hats. "I'm not good at the claw machines, but I really wanted the hats, so I thought, 'Well, let's just knit them.'" "I see," Miyamoto replied. "I'm also bad at the claw machines." That was a close one! Watch Hello! Pikmin short movies and enjoy new Pikmin adventures. https://t.co/8OPB48hDZr The Pikmin Day Direct also featured a brand-new Pikmin Original Short Movie. Following last year's Close to You short, this video sees a Red Pikmin do its best to grab a baseball from a frog. It's as cute as you could ever expect. As part of Nintendo's initiative to lean harder into the series, new shorts will be released monthly via the Nintendo Today! app, as well as other channels. However, there will also be a new episode released tomorrow, with another set to follow sometime in November. Miyamoto said he's collaborating with Nintendo Pictures staff to make the shorts. That's all for the Pikmin Day Direct. While there was no hint at anything like Pikmin 5, planting November 1 as an official holiday is probably a sign that Nintendo has no intention of putting a cap on Pikmin content anytime soon. While we wait for any bigger updates on the franchise, you can check out IGN's 9/10 Pikmin 4 review . Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

sources.title: Shigeru Miyamoto Declares November 1st Pikmin Day In Surprise Nintendo Direct
sources.text: Nintendo Nintendo Direct Pikmin Pikmin 4 pikmin bloom Anything can happen on Halloween. A dog can turn into a cat. Canada can eliminate daylight savings . Shigeru Miyamoto can drop a new holiday altogether. This morning, Nintendo announced a spur of the moment Nintendo Direct. In it, Miyamoto declares that tomorrow, November 1st, will henceforth be known as ‘ Pikmin Day.’ While the Direct had updates for two of the most recent Olimar adventures, it did not provide information about any new games. “Starting this year, we’re going to start calling November 1st Pikmin Day,” says Miyamoto behind a banner of clovers and distant Pikmin chants . “Going forward, I want people to know more about Pikmin .” Released on the GameCube in the fall of 2001, the original Pikmin only debuted around this time of year. Miyamotoâs reasoning is that if three Pikmin stood shoulder to shoulder, they would resemble the date ‘11.1.’ Though this conflicts with the Day of the Dead, experienced players know there are probably some deceased Pikmin spirits you could atone to. It doesnât hurt that in two weeks, the Nintendo Switch 2 edition of Pikmin 4 will drop. While the surprise Direct didnât provide any surprise new games, it did bring information on what the new edition will offer, plus an update on the mobile Pikmin Bloom . Using the built-in microphone, the Switch 2 version of Pikmin 4 will allow you to command your pooch-like assistant Oatchi vocal instructions. Hopefully more dependably than what Hey You, Pikachu! could pull off . The new version will also feature an exclusive new mode, ‘Dandori Academy,’ a timed treasure rush. You will only get one try in this mode on Friday through Sunday, where your score will be submitted, but you will be allowed to practice and hone the trial through the upcoming week. A demo for this new mode will be available on Monday, ahead of the November 12th launch. As for Pikmin Bloom , the Pikminâs even tinier adventure, youâll soon be able to send your lil’ dudes underground. Caves are being added to the mobile game. Akin to the gauntlets of the console series, these caves promise heaps of treasure at the risk of total Pikmin devastation. The direct ended on a new animated Pikmin short, adding that the once mysterious cartoons will soon be a monthly occurrence. Miyamoto also introduced actress and Pikmin ambassador Fuka Koshiba, who caught his eye crocheting hats. Happy Pikmin Day eve, everyone. I hope you are doing well.
